outcomes: A Claude Code or Codex session publishes its state, plan, delivered messages, decisions and replies to its mission through the missions contract, from the host hooks @putnami/contributor declares
The agent receives its mission sheet at session start and the owner's messages and answers at the end of a turn or during a wait
nonGoals: Writing the host files: the core writes the hooks the manifest declares
Choosing or falling back to a missions provider
Changing host permissions, credentials or model access

requirements.text: SessionStart syncs the session, reads the mission's checkpoint through memory.mission when memory is bound, and prints the mission sheet: the repository and key missions.ask takes, the title, the plan, the open decisions and the checkpoint, within 4 KiB, with every agent or owner text quoted with "> ". Waiting messages follow whole while the context stays within 9,500 bytes. A sheet the provider did not refresh says its date; a workspace without missions gets none.

PostToolUse records a TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate or update_plan plan change, the id of a decision missions.ask opened, and a marker for a reply missions.reply recorded or found closed. It runs no git and calls no provider, ignores a subagent's plan, and spools the call when another hook holds the session lock. A recorded reply wins over an ack line for the same message.

Stop sends the state, the changed plan, the delivered message ids, the asked decisions and the [ack <id>] lines of the last message in one sync. A waiting message continues the turn once: additional context on Claude Code, a block on Codex. A message is delivered once the hook wrote it; the next sync reports it, and a hook stopped before keeps it for the next. A Codex Stop waits up to 180 s only for an open decision this session asked. StopFailure publishes the error. A refused reply is dropped for good.

The Claude Code idle wake pairs with the Stop of its own event, waits only when that Stop did not continue the turn, syncs at the provider's pace within 5 s to 10 min, and ends after 10 minutes or when a new turn starts. It exits 75 with the message on stderr only when a message waits, and never waits for an SDK host.

Every hook path other than a waking idle wake exits 0. A failure, a missing host channel, a bad payload or an outcome other than ok prints no error and leaves one line in hook.log, which rotates at 1 MiB. A failed call closes the channel so the next one dials again, and what the sync did not deliver stays queued. A plan the provider refuses goes once without it.

Each event stops 5 s before the timeout its manifest entry declares, each call takes at most 10 s of what is left, and the common longest path of each event, its git commands, calls and waits, fits that budget.

A session reports to issue-<n> once agent attach --issue <n> declared it for the checkout and branch, else to branch:<branch>. The repository is the lowercase owner/name of the origin remote, without host or credential; a local path or a remote without an owner names none. The session store lives under the Putnami home, never in the checkout.
The executable behind putnami agent hook reaches the missions and memory providers only through the host RPC channel putnami opens for the interactive launch.
